YouTube révolutionne son système de comp: YouTube is revolutionizing its view-counting system with a major redesign announced for August 24, 2026. From now on, every view will be recorded as soon as the video starts, harmonizing the rules for long-form content and Shorts. This decision impacts creators and developers alike, as well as recommendation algorithms.
Jusqu’à présent, une vue n’était validée: Until now, a view was only validated after 30 seconds for long videos and live streams, whereas Shorts had been counted from their launch since 2025. Starting August 24, 2026, this distinction will disappear: every view will be recorded instantly upon startup. YouTube justifies this harmonization to align with industry standards (TikTok, Instagram Reels) and clarify metrics, thus avoiding confusion between genuine engagement and a simple click.
Les algorithmes de monétisation et de re: Monetization and recommendation algorithms will continue to take genuine engagement into account to assess content quality.
Les développeurs doivent adapter leurs i: Developers must adapt their integrations across three key interfaces: YouTube Data API, YouTube Analytics API, and Reporting API. The public viewCount field will switch to the new count without historical recalculation. To preserve retention analysis, YouTube is introducing a complementary metric: engagedViews, which retains the former 30-second threshold to accurately compare performance before and after the redesign. This distinction will allow creators to measure the real impact of their content on engagement, independently of instant views.
Si les créateurs anticipent une hausse m: While creators anticipate a mechanical increase in the view counter, YouTube reminds them that genuine engagement (watch time, likes, comments) remains the sole lever for monetization and algorithmic recommendation. To succeed in this new landscape, optimizing the first few seconds (striking thumbnail, clear hook) becomes crucial: an audience quick to click away demands captivating content from the very first glance. Algorithms will favor videos generating a high retention rate, even if their view count increases artificially thanks to the new system.
